original_question: If an F-division algebra has prime period, must it be a crossed product? In other words, for each prime p, is every central division algebra whose Brauer class has order p necessarily obtained from a Galois crossed-product construction?
target_in_paper: §2, Problem 2.1, "Other problems regarding crossed products": "Determine whether F-division algebras of prime period are crossed products."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets the prime-period crossed-product problem, not the neighboring prime-degree cyclicity problem. It already has the right ambient setting of a division algebra over a field F, correctly interprets "prime period" as the Brauer-class order being a prime p, and correctly asks whether such algebras must come from crossed-product/Galois data rather than asking for cyclicity.
missing_details: In the paper, an "F-division algebra" means a finite-dimensional central division algebra over F, not an arbitrary division ring.
The quantifier is over all base fields F and all prime periods; the paper does not fix a special field unless explicitly stated.
The period is defined as the order of the Brauer class [D] in Br(F).
The paper's definition of "crossed product" is: the algebra contains a maximal torus that is Galois over F; for a division algebra, this is equivalently a maximal subfield K/F that is Galois.
The problem asks only whether such algebras are crossed products for some finite Galois extension; it does not ask for cyclic crossed products or for any specified Galois group.
No restriction on degree or index is part of Problem 2.1; the issue is specifically prime period, not prime degree.
refined_question: Let F be a field, and let D be a finite-dimensional central division algebra over F. If the period per(D), i.e. the order of its Brauer class [D] in Br(F), is a prime number p, must D be a crossed product? Equivalently, must D contain a maximal subfield K such that K/F is Galois?
equivalent_formulation: For every field F and every central F-division algebra D with prime period, does D contain a maximal subfield that is Galois over F?
justification: This is Problem 2.1 in §2, not Problem 1.1: the draft asks about prime period and crossed products, whereas Problem 1.1 asks for non-cyclic division algebras of prime degree. To make the question stand alone while staying paper-faithful, the hidden definitions had to be imported from §0: period means the order of [D] in Br(F), and crossed product means containing a maximal torus Galois over F; for division algebras this becomes a maximal subfield Galois over F. I therefore kept the scope exactly at arbitrary F-division algebras of prime period, without adding any degree, index, characteristic, or roots-of-unity assumptions.
